entities.summary:
Cleonaeus was a Rhodian admiral who played a pivotal role in the Battle of Chios (c. 222 BCE) and the Battle of Lade (c. 208 BCE). He was second-in-command to Theophiliscus at the Battle of Chios, but after Theophiliscus' death from his wounds, Cleonaeus took command and led the Rhodian fleet to victory. However, he was defeated by Philip V of Macedon at the Battle of Lade while sailing back to Rhodes.


Cleonaeus' actions had significant consequences for the Hellenistic world, as the Rhodian fleet's victory at the Battle of Chios helped to secure the region's independence from Macedonian rule. The defeat at the Battle of Lade, on the other hand, marked a turning point in the Rhodian-Macedonian conflict and led to the Rhodians' eventual surrender to Philip V.


The legacy of Cleonaeus can be seen in the later history of the Rhodian fleet, which continued to play a significant role in the Hellenistic world. His military campaigns and strategic decisions also influenced the development of the Rhodian city-state and its relationships with other Hellenistic powers.


In the end, Cleonaeus' story serves as a testament to the complexities and uncertainties of ancient Greek warfare, where even the most skilled and experienced leaders could fall victim to the whims of fate and the machinations of their rivals.
